title: Fourier coefficient of the binary generator density
statement: Let $\ell>0$, and let a monic polynomial of degree $\ell$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ be specified by its lower coefficients and assumed irreducible. For every $n$-coordinate binary vector $\gamma$, its vector Fourier coefficient under the distribution obtained by choosing the generator’s two seeds uniformly is the number of roots $r\in\mathbb{F}_2^\ell$ of the finite-field sum formed from the coordinates of $\gamma$ and the successive powers of the first seed, divided by $2^\ell$.
hypotheses_covered: The specified monic binary polynomial is irreducible
caveat: The statement uses a recursively defined modular multiplication and power-sum construction; its exact algebraic meaning depends on those definitions.
